findings.text: When the captured stack has fewer than two newlines, `stackWithoutTwoTopLines` becomes '' and `endsWith('')` is always true, so the async stack is never appended. The original regex left the string unchanged when it didn't match, so it compared the full stack and still appended. Failing input: `dummy.stack` is 'Error\n    at foo' (the sliced stack is one line) and `err.stack` is a different existing stack. The original appends the frame and the new code silently drops it.
